title: DHCP Concepts Practice
subject: DHCP
description: Practice troubleshooting common DHCP problems using evidence-first triage, diagnosis, and fix decisions. Titles and summaries are symptom-based so the workflow reveals the root cause.
reportOverview: This report summarizes your ticket outcomes and change notes for DHCP concepts practice. Use it to reinforce what evidence led you to each decision.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Read the observed symptom and scan the evidence.
2) Decide what you should verify first (Triage).
3) Choose the most likely cause based on the evidence (Diagnosis).
4) Select the best remediation action (Fix).
5) Write a short change note describing what changed and how you validated it.

tickets.title: New DHCP server shows running but clients cannot obtain leases
tickets.summary: A newly installed DHCP server shows the service as running, but the DHCP console shows a red down arrow and clients cannot obtain IP addresses from it.
artifact: "The DHCP service is not authorized to start."
validations: Confirm DHCP server is authorized in AD.
Confirm console icon turns normal and leases issue.
Renew a client lease successfully.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the new DHCP server?
options: Whether the DHCP server is authorized in Active Directory
Whether the client NIC driver is updated
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether DNS scavenging is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause given Event ID 1046?
options: The DHCP server is not authorized in Active Directory
The DHCP scope is exhausted
The gateway option is incorrect
The client has a stale DNS cache

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Authorize the DHCP server in the DHCP console (or via AD) and restart the DHCP service if required
Create a CNAME record for the DHCP server
Disable secure dynamic updates in DNS
Reduce DHCP lease time to 5 minutes

tickets.title: New computers can reach internal hosts by IP but cannot use names
tickets.summary: A new batch of computers can ping internal servers by IP address, but they cannot resolve internal names or complete domain-related tasks.
validations: Confirm clients receive DNS server IPs via DHCP.
Confirm nslookup resolves internal names.
Confirm domain operations proceed normally.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST in the DHCP scope settings?
options: Scope Option 006 (DNS Servers) is configured with internal DNS/DC IPs
Scope lease duration is 8 days
Scope has an exclusion range
DHCP failover is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause of the symptom?
options: The scope is missing DNS server option(s), so clients have no DNS resolver configured
The DNS zone transfer is blocked
A root zone named "." exists
Clients are using stale resolver cache

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Configure DHCP Option 006 with the correct internal DNS server IPs and renew client leases
Create a reverse lookup zone
Disable DHCP on the server
Change the workstation hostname

tickets.title: New arrivals cannot get internet after the office fills up
tickets.summary: Early arrivals have working connectivity, but later arrivals cannot get online and show limited connectivity on their devices.
artifact: Client IP becomes 169.254.x.x (APIPA) after renew attempts
validations: Confirm address availability increases after remediation.
Renew on multiple clients succeeds.
Monitor scope utilization stays below capacity.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST on the DHCP server?
options: Scope address utilization and available addresses
DNS forwarders configuration
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether DHCP audit logging is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause given the evidence?
options: The DHCP scope does not have free addresses available
A CNAME record is missing
The DHCP server is unauthorized
Clients are using public DNS

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Expand the scope range (or add capacity) and consider adjusting lease duration appropriately
Create a new forward lookup zone
Disable secure dynamic updates
Create a root zone named "."

tickets.title: Laptop works on Wi-Fi but fails to get an address when docked
tickets.summary: A laptop receives a valid IP address on Wi-Fi, but when connected via a docking station it fails to obtain an IP address.
artifact: An Allow filter is enabled on the DHCP server.
Wi-Fi MAC is present in Allow list; dock MAC is not.
validations: Confirm dock MAC is included where needed.
Renew succeeds while docked.
Confirm correct scope/options are applied.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the DHCP server?
options: Whether DHCP filtering is enabled and if the dock MAC is permitted
Whether DNS forwarders exist
Whether scavenging is enabled
Whether a reverse lookup zone exists

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The docking station NIC has a different MAC address that is not allowed by DHCP filtering
The DHCP scope is exhausted
The subnet mask is incorrect on the scope
The DNS server is missing a CNAME

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Add the docking station MAC to the Allow filter (or disable overly restrictive filtering) and renew the lease
Create a new DHCP scope for Wi-Fi only
Delete all reservations
Change the DNS zone type to Secondary

tickets.title: A user receives an unexpected address range and cannot access internal resources
tickets.summary: A user’s computer shows it is connected, but it receives an IP address that does not match the organization’s addressing and cannot access internal resources.
validations: Confirm authorized DHCP servers are the only responders.
Renew results in an organizational IP range.
Consider preventive controls (e.g., switch protections) where appropriate.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST based on the client evidence?
options: Identify which device is acting as the DHCP server (192.168.1.1) and where it is connected
Create a reverse lookup zone for 192.168.1.0/24
Add DNS forwarders to the DC
Change the DHCP lease time to 1 hour

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause?
options: An unauthorized DHCP device is issuing leases on the network
The DNS client cache is stale
The DHCP server is not authorized in AD
The subnet mask was typed incorrectly in the DHCP scope

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Locate and remove/disable the unauthorized DHCP device, then renew the client lease
Delete the contoso.com DNS zone
Disable secure dynamic updates
Convert the DHCP scope into a superscope

tickets.title: DHCP console flags a specific address as unusable after repeated conflicts
tickets.summary: A specific IP address keeps being marked as unusable in the DHCP console, and clients sometimes report IP conflicts.
artifact: A printer is configured manually with a static IP address.
validations: Confirm the static device IP is excluded from the DHCP pool.
Remove conflict entry if appropriate and observe it does not return.
Verify clients no longer report IP conflict warnings.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST to stop repeated IP conflicts?
options: Whether any device is using a static IP inside the DHCP dynamic range
Whether DNS forwarders are configured
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether DHCP is authorized in AD

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A static IP device is using an address in the DHCP pool, causing conflicts
The DHCP server binding is incorrect
The DHCP lease time is too long
Clients are using public DNS

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Add an exclusion for the static device IP (or move the static device outside the DHCP range), then clear the conflict entry
Create a new DNS CNAME record
Enable scavenging on DNS
Delete the DHCP scope and recreate it with the same range

tickets.title: Clients on a different VLAN cannot obtain addresses while others can
tickets.summary: Clients on one floor (separate VLAN/subnet) cannot obtain DHCP addresses, while clients on the same VLAN as the server work normally.
artifact: Clients on Floor-2 VLAN get 169.254.x.x after renew attempts.
Clients on Floor-1 VLAN obtain leases normally.
No requests appear from the Floor-2 subnet in DHCP logs.
validations: Confirm DHCP relay/helper is configured for the VLAN interface.
Confirm DORA exchange completes for Floor-2 clients.
Renew succeeds on Floor-2 clients.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST for DHCP across VLANs?
options: DHCP relay / IP helper configuration on the router or Layer-3 interface
DNS forwarders configuration
Whether the DHCP server is authorized
Whether a reverse lookup zone exists

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause based on the evidence?
options: DHCP broadcasts are not being relayed from the VLAN/subnet to the DHCP server
The DHCP scope is exhausted
Clients are using a stale DNS cache
The DNS zone is configured as Secondary

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Configure the correct IP helper/relay address for that VLAN interface and retest renew
Disable DHCP on all switches
Change the DHCP scope to a /16 subnet
Create a root zone named "."

tickets.title: DHCP redundancy does not take over when one server is down
tickets.summary: One DHCP server is down, but clients are not obtaining leases from the second server as expected. The failover status shows an error state.
artifact: DHCP failover status on partner server:
When DHCP1 is stopped, new clients fail to obtain leases.
validations: Confirm failover relationship shows healthy/normal state.
Confirm leases issue while one partner is down.
Confirm lease replication behaves normally.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST in a DHCP failover issue where takeover fails?
options: The failover relationship health and authentication (shared secret) between partners
Whether DNS forwarders are configured
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether the subnet mask is correct in DNS

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause given the evidence?
options: The failover relationship is not functioning correctly (authentication/config mismatch), preventing partner takeover
The DHCP scope is exhausted
Clients are using public DNS
A CNAME record is missing

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Reconfigure/recreate the failover relationship with matching settings and shared secret, then resync
Disable DHCP on the second server
Delete all DHCP scopes
Enable DNS scavenging

tickets.title: Reservation was updated but the client keeps using the old address
tickets.summary: An administrator changed a reservation to a new IP, but the client continues to use the previous IP address.
artifact: - Address Leases show an active lease for 10.0.0.50 for the same MAC
validations: Confirm the old lease is released/cleared as appropriate.
Renew results in the reserved address.
Confirm no duplicate reservation/lease remains.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST when a client ignores a new reservation?
options: Whether the old lease is still active for that client identifier (MAC) and needs renewal/release
Whether DNS forwarders are configured
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether DHCP is unauthorized in AD

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely reason the client keeps the old IP?
options: The client still holds an active lease for the old address and has not renewed/released yet
The DNS server has a root zone named "."
The DHCP scope is exhausted
The subnet mask is wrong on the client

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Force the client to release/renew (or clear the old lease) so it can obtain the updated reserved address
Delete the reservation permanently
Disable DHCP failover
Move the client to a different VLAN without changes

tickets.title: Clients can talk locally but not beyond their subnet after a scope change
tickets.summary: Clients receive an IP address but cannot communicate outside their immediate subnet segment. Only a small group of hosts are reachable.
artifact: Servers reside on 10.0.0.0/16 and should be reachable from this segment.
validations: Confirm clients receive correct mask after remediation.
Confirm clients can reach intended subnets.
Confirm scope configuration matches network design.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the client configuration obtained from DHCP?
options: The subnet mask provided by the DHCP scope
Whether DNS forwarders exist
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether the client has a stale DNS cache

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause of limited connectivity given the evidence?
options: The DHCP scope is providing an incorrect subnet mask for the network design
The DHCP server is unauthorized
A CNAME record is missing
DNS scavenging deleted records

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Correct the DHCP scope configuration by recreating it with the proper subnet mask, then renew clients
Add 8.8.8.8 as a DNS forwarder
Create a root zone named "."
Disable secure dynamic updates
